Appraises a helium recovery system from its cost, yearly gas saving, running cost and life, giving NPV, IRR and payback at two helium prices to test the purchase.
Gives the mean velocity from a flow and the internal bore, the first check on any meter reading: 200 L/min of wort in a 47.8 mm bore moves at 1.858 m/s.

Converts gas flows between pressures and temperatures, turning a compressor's free air rating into the actual volume a vortex meter senses at 7 bar gauge, and back.
Shows the root-sum-square uncertainty method for a gauge; the chapter applies the same steps in percentages to an orifice meter's coefficient, bore, differential and density.
Charts a daily water balance residual with moving-range control limits; two days outside the limits revealed a buried leak of about 2 m³ a day.
Appraises meter decisions from cost, yearly benefit, life and hurdle rate: replacing an orifice plate does not pay, while a low-flow meter that reveals air leaks pays back in under two years.
Values compressed-air leakage from a measured leak flow, compressor specific power, hours and electricity price: 10 L/s of free air costs about A$10,200 a year.
